But someone I didn't expect to meet was Avinash Sooriyarachchi, one of Mistral’s researchers, who flew in from San Francisco to speak at the event. So naturally, I told him about the API error

Notify just got its first real users! It's been a week since my last post, and I'm excited to share that Notify has gained 3 real users since then, and by "real users," I mean people I don't know at all, who found and signed up for Notify on their own, and are actively using it to help them study. Right now, we're just taking it slow, but we're gaining momentum. If you're taking some note-heavy or tough courses with your friends this semester, give Notify a try: notifyy.ca

I was sitting in class when I got a text from a friend: “Yo, are you notifying this?” School just started, and Notify is already getting its first users. So far, all of them have been personal friends, which is honestly still pretty exciting to see. But mark my words: it won’t be long before students I’ve never met start adopting it too. This is just the beginning.

Why do we still gatekeep notes? Every class has someone with the "good notes." Everyone asks them for the Google Doc a day before the exam. But the best notes should come from the whole class. So I built Notify, a platform where everyone in a class uploads their notes, and they get merged into one comprehensive set that everyone can learn from.
